headline: PM Tarique Rahman leaves Dalian for Beijing to begin state visit
summary: After attending the World Economic Forum's 'Summer Davos' in Dalian, the Prime Minister departs for the Chinese capital for high-level bilateral meetings.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has departed Dalian via high-speed train to begin a three-day state visit to Beijing, accompanied by his wife, Zubaida Rahman.
The Prime Minister had been attending the 17th annual World Economic Forum (WEF) 'Meeting of the New Champions' conference, often referred to as the 'summer-time Davos'.
The WEF session featured over 1,700 representatives from 90 countries, including the Prime Ministers of China, South Korea, Kazakhstan, Mongolia, Montenegro, and Guinea.
During the conference, PM Tarique spoke at a session titled 'Climate Leadership in a Shifting Global Landscape' and met with WEF President and CEO Alois Zwinggi.
In Beijing, the Prime Minister is scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Thursday and Friday.
He will also meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and other top leaders of the Chinese Communist Party during his stay.
The Prime Minister's Office stated that his participation in the 'Summer Davos' aims to expand investment and employment opportunities for Bangladesh and adopt global best practices.
The visit follows his first foreign trip to Malaysia, marking a continued effort to strengthen international diplomatic ties.
caption:
From the 'Summer Davos' to the capital. PM Tarique Rahman heads to Beijing for a high-level state visit.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has departed Dalian via high-speed train to begin a three-day state visit to Beijing, accompanied by his wife, Zubaida Rahman.

The Prime Minister had been attending the 17th annual World Economic Forum (WEF) 'Meeting of the New Champions' conference, often referred to as the 'summer-time Davos'.

The WEF session featured over 1,700 representatives from 90 countries, including the Prime Ministers of China, South Korea, Kazakhstan, Mongolia, Montenegro, and Guinea.

During the conference, PM Tarique spoke at a session titled 'Climate Leadership in a Shifting Global Landscape' and met with WEF President and CEO Alois Zwinggi.

In Beijing, the Prime Minister is scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Thursday and Friday.

He will also meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and other top leaders of the Chinese Communist Party during his stay.

The Prime Minister's Office stated that his participation in the 'Summer Davos' aims to expand investment and employment opportunities for Bangladesh and adopt global best practices.

The visit follows his first foreign trip to Malaysia, marking a continued effort to strengthen international diplomatic ties.

headline_marked: Lawyer files writ to [[challenge ICT Act legality]], calling it a tool for 'judicial killings'
headline: Lawyer files writ to challenge ICT Act legality, calling it a tool for 'judicial killings'
summary: A Supreme Court lawyer has petitioned the High Court to annul the International Crimes Tribunal Act, arguing it is unconstitutional and unlawful.
details: A Supreme Court lawyer, Muhammed Mohshen Rashid, has filed a writ petition challenging the legality of the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Act, seeking its complete annulment.
Rashid, who is also the president of a faction of the Bangladesh Muslim League, describes the law as unconstitutional and characterizes the tribunal as an instrument of "judicial killings."
He argues that the 2009 amendments to the ICT law were used to carry out executions, and that changes made in 2024 have further reinforced this role.
The petitioner claims the tribunal has become a mechanism for executing people through judicial proceedings and expresses concern that the law could be used against those currently in power.
The ICT Act was originally enacted in 1973 to prosecute crimes against humanity committed during the 1971 Liberation War.
The law was amended in 2009 to allow the prosecution of both individuals and organizations, leading to trials of senior Jamaat-e-Islami leaders.
Following the fall of the Awami League government in 2024, the interim administration used the same tribunal to prosecute alleged crimes against humanity linked to the July movement.
Since the tribunal's reconstitution, verdicts have been delivered in four cases, with ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and 12 others sentenced to death.
caption:
Is the ICT Act unconstitutional? A lawyer has petitioned the High Court to abolish the tribunal, calling it a tool for 'judicial killings'.

A Supreme Court lawyer, Muhammed Mohshen Rashid, has filed a writ petition challenging the legality of the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Act, seeking its complete annulment.

Rashid, who is also the president of a faction of the Bangladesh Muslim League, describes the law as unconstitutional and characterizes the tribunal as an instrument of "judicial killings."

He argues that the 2009 amendments to the ICT law were used to carry out executions, and that changes made in 2024 have further reinforced this role.

The petitioner claims the tribunal has become a mechanism for executing people through judicial proceedings and expresses concern that the law could be used against those currently in power.

The ICT Act was originally enacted in 1973 to prosecute crimes against humanity committed during the 1971 Liberation War.

The law was amended in 2009 to allow the prosecution of both individuals and organizations, leading to trials of senior Jamaat-e-Islami leaders.

Following the fall of the Awami League government in 2024, the interim administration used the same tribunal to prosecute alleged crimes against humanity linked to the July movement.

Since the tribunal's reconstitution, verdicts have been delivered in four cases, with ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and 12 others sentenced to death.
